Spoil heaps run down the hillside in grey fans the heather has never taken. Above them a timbered mouth opens into the hill. Cut into the beam in the old script, worn but whole: LAPISORATIO.
The heather stops a long stride short of the adit mouth all round, scorched back, and grows again beyond. Nothing nests in the spoil.

The last of the spoil, at the top of the heap, is not the same stone as the rest. It is black and glassy, as if fired. The Delvers’ last gallery broke into something that was not rock.

The steps come out on a ledge, and your light goes out into nothing. Below you is a hall that could hold the whole of Windworth, its pillars going down further than the light does, and far down water lies still. Nobody in Windworth knows it is here.
